title: One-year outcomes of microhook trabeculotomy versus suture trabeculotomy ab interno

license.statement: CC BY 4.0 (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License)

indication: open-angle glaucoma (primary open-angle, exfoliative, steroid-induced and other open-angle glaucoma) without previous glaucoma surgery; gonioscopy-assisted suture trabeculotomy ab interno (S-LOT, attempted 360 degrees) or Tanito microhook trabeculotomy (two to three quadrants), each with or without simultaneous phacoemulsification; retrospective single-centre study, more than 12 months of follow-up required; some patients contributed both eyes

groups.description: Suture trabeculotomy ab interno with phacoemulsification (Table 2 row R5)
Microhook trabeculotomy with phacoemulsification (Table 2 row R6)
Suture trabeculotomy ab interno without phacoemulsification (Table 2 row R8)
Microhook trabeculotomy without phacoemulsification (Table 2 row R9)

cells 'mean (median) ± SD (n = k)': leading mean used; per-visit n inside each cell

Attrition: per-visit n declines in every subgroup although inclusion required more than 12 months of follow-up; 11 S-group and 4 µ-group eyes had additional glaucoma surgery (Results). The article does not state whether eyes were removed from the means after additional surgery, so the series are kept as attrition under the protocol; flagged for review.
Role: two established ab interno trabeculotomy techniques compared retrospectively; all groups are recorded as control.
Hyphema washout was performed in some eyes for uncontrolled IOP elevation (Results); not an exclusion.
